$comment: End-to-end tasks for comparing how agents get @tecton/react context. Each task is one file an agent writes; `expect` is what a correct solution contains: `import` = that name (or one of its `|`-separated aliases) imported from that module, `jsx` + `prop` = that element carries one of the `|`-separated props. Graded by agent-eval/grade.mjs.

tasks.prompt: Write `WellsTable.tsx` exporting `WellsTable({ wells, onCreate }: { wells: Array<{ id: string; name: string; field: string; status: "producing" | "shut-in" | "drilling"; updatedAt: string }>; onCreate: () => void })`. It renders a table of wells with the columns name, field, status and last updated. Status is shown as a coloured status label: producing = success, shut-in = warning, drilling = info. When `wells` is empty, show a proper empty state explaining there are no wells yet, with a button that creates one. Above the table, a "New well" button with a well icon calls `onCreate`.

Write `DeleteWellButton.tsx` exporting `DeleteWellButton({ wellId, wellName, deleteWell }: { wellId: string; wellName: string; deleteWell: (id: string) => Promise<void> })`. A destructive "Delete" button asks the user to confirm before deleting, because it cannot be undone. On confirm, call `deleteWell` and then show a brief, transient success confirmation that the well was deleted.

Write `WellSettingsForm.tsx` exporting `WellSettingsForm({ onSave }: { onSave: (values: { name: string; operator: string; notify: boolean; notes: string }) => Promise<void> })`. Fields: well name (text), operator (pick one of Equinor, Aker BP, Vår Energi, ConocoPhillips), "Notify me on alarms" (an on/off setting), and notes (multi-line text). Every field has a visible label. The Save button is disabled while saving.

Write `HorizonFilter.tsx` exporting `HorizonFilter({ horizons, selected, onChange }: { horizons: string[]; selected: string[]; onChange: (next: string[]) => void })`. Show the horizons as toggleable filter tags, of which the user can select several. Below them, show the currently active filters as tags that can each be removed.

Write `ProductionKpis.tsx` exporting `ProductionKpis({ oilRate, gasRate, waterCut }: { oilRate: { value: number; change: number }; gasRate: { value: number; change: number }; waterCut: { value: number; change: number } })`. Show the three KPIs in a row — oil rate in Sm³/d, gas rate in MSm³/d, water cut in % — each with its change versus last month. If water cut is above 30 %, show a warning message above the row that stays on the page.

Write `WellDetails.tsx` exporting `WellDetails({ well }: { well: { name: string; operator: string; spudDate: string; depthM: number; logs: string[] } })`. A "Details" button opens a panel that slides in from the right edge of the screen, with the well's name as its title and two tabs: "Overview" (operator, spud date, depth) and "Logs" (the list of log names). Keep both the open state and the selected tab in React state.

Write `SeismicToolbar.tsx` exporting `SeismicToolbar({ onZoomIn, onZoomOut, onReset, showFaults, onShowFaultsChange, onExport }: { onZoomIn: () => void; onZoomOut: () => void; onReset: () => void; showFaults: boolean; onShowFaultsChange: (show: boolean) => void; onExport: (format: "png" | "segy") => void })`. A compact toolbar with: three icon-only buttons (zoom in, zoom out, reset view), each with a tooltip; a toggle button "Show faults" with the fault icon; and an "Export" dropdown menu with "PNG image" and "SEG-Y".

Write `LogCurvesPanel.tsx` exporting `LogCurvesPanel({ state, curves, uploadProgress, onRetry }: { state: "loading" | "error" | "ready"; curves: string[]; uploadProgress: number | null; onRetry: () => void })`. While loading, show placeholders shaped like the list rows. On error, show an error message that stays on the page with a Retry action. When ready, list the curve names. When `uploadProgress` is a number, show the progress of that upload (0–100), which the user is watching, above the list.
